insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as multiplier benefit irrespective of any claims... The maximum multiplier bonus will not exceed 100% of the Basic Sum Insured in any Policy Year.”
great.explanation: A 10% multiplier benefit is added on every renewal without break, irrespective of any claims, up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured. Your coverage can grow over time even if you claim, which is better than typical NCBs that reduce or reset after a claim.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: “Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement...” (definition present, but no co-pay percentage/trigger stated in benefits/conditions in provided extract).
great.explanation: Only a co-payment definition is present and no applied co-pay clause/trigger is shown in the provided extract. No co-pay is charged based on the available wording, so admissible claims should be paid at 100% (subject to other terms).

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “30-day waiting period... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.”
good.explanation: Listed diseases/surgeries are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. Claims for these conditions in the first 2 years can be rejected even if the illness is newly diagnosed.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage. You should expect out-of-pocket costs for PED-related treatment during the first 3 policy years.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses... incurred upto 60 days before the date of admission to the Hospital”
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospital admission are covered if related to the hospitalization. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses... incurred upto 90 days after discharge from Hospitalisation”
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 90 days after discharge are covered if related to the hospitalization. This supports follow-up visits, diagnostics, and medicines after you leave the hospital.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: No restore/reinstatement benefit wording found in the provided document text.
bad.reference: Not mentioned in provided pages (Policy Wording extract)
bad.explanation: No restore/reinstatement of Sum Insured is mentioned in the provided extract. After using your Sum Insured, you may not get an automatic refill for later hospitalizations in the same policy year.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Annexure I - List I - Items for which coverage is not available in the policy... GLOVES... MASK... NEBULISATION KIT... ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]”
bad.explanation: Many common consumables (e.g., gloves, masks, nebulisation kit, and various procedure kits) are not covered. These can add meaningful out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization.

bad.name: Ambulance Cover
bad.explanation: Ambulance expenses are capped at ₹2,000 per hospitalization. You may have to pay the balance if actual ambulance charges are higher.

unclear.explanation: No room rent limit/eligibility is visible in the provided extract. Room rent terms matter because a cap can lead to proportionate deductions across the entire hospital bill.
